primary_claim: Testing unsupervised elicitation (UE) and easy-to-hard (E2H) generalization techniques on new realistic stress-test datasets targeting three challenges (salient non-truth features, imbalanced training sets, and impossible/normative tasks), the authors find that no existing or newly proposed technique (including ensembling and UE+E2H combination) reliably solves all three challenges: accuracy degrades sharply with highly salient spurious features (e.g. sycophancy, political leaning, toxicity), UE methods surprisingly tolerate imbalance well on GSM8K but perform poorly on the more realistic Ctrl-Z bash-command dataset, and methods are often as confident or more confident on normative political questions as on objective math questions.

effect.metric: classification accuracy / AUROC under salient-feature, imbalance, and impossible-task perturbations
effect.value: accuracy degrades sharply for highly salient spurious features (sycophancy) vs. minimal degradation for low-salience features (tense); on GSM8K performance at ~0% correct training labels is at least as good as balanced data for several methods, but Ctrl-Z shows performance degrading further under imbalance from an already-low balanced baseline (~50% due to salient non-truth features like answer length); UE/E2H methods often equally or more confident on normative political claims than on GSM8K

contradicts_or_qualifies: Extends Farquhar et al.'s demonstration that CCS can fail on salient non-truth features to more diverse, realistic datasets
The conceptual expectation that imbalanced training sets should hurt CCS-style probing methods; authors find GSM8K performance is often robust to imbalance contrary to this expectation
stated_future_work: Benchmark SFT-based methods and weak-to-strong generalization methods not covered in this work
Explore rebalancing strategies using a weak classifier (e.g. zero-shot) to get rough training labels for resampling, while noting this could itself run into the same challenges
Study challenges from scheming AIs that might intentionally interfere with elicitation methods
Explore more sophisticated consistency properties beyond CCS and bootstrapping
Build evaluation datasets that capture challenges of the most important UE applications for future method development
limitations_stated: Analysis covers a representative but not exhaustive range of UE and E2H methods; did not benchmark SFT-based or weak-to-strong generalization methods
Some datasets are not fully realistic (e.g. mixing GSM8K with normative political claims creates an unrealistic distribution shift that let some methods just differentiate by dataset origin)
Does not address scheming AIs intentionally interfering with elicitation

Unsupervised elicitation failures may remain silent until catastrophic, since by definition in-distribution ground truth is unavailable for the intended real-world applications, making evaluation itself difficult
quote: We find that although the new hopes sometimes perform better than other approaches, no technique reliably performs well on the 3 challenges.
